You need candidates for a planned test. On cost per task the field is wide: the cheapest tracked option is MiMo-V2.6-Pro at 0.26 $, and the dearest is Gemini 3.8 Flash at 6.26 $.

### Sources and dates for the model comparison

For cost per task, the source is Artificial Analysis, which prices one Intelligence Index task on each model. Inkling 2 Small costs 1.18 $, so MiMo-V2.6-Pro is about a quarter of that.

At 2.19 $, Nemotron 3 Ultra costs nearly double Inkling's price. Gemini 3.8 Flash costs 6.26 $, more than five times Inkling's, so a switch there raises the bill. [...] ### Which Inkling 2 Small alternative fits your team

By itself, none of these would have prevented the failure, because each has its own limit that a different workload will hit. MiMo-V2.6-Pro at 0.26 $ is the cheapest, but cheapest isn't safest.

What would have prevented the failure is a tested fallback and a written rule for when to switch to it. Pick the candidate whose limit your workload never reaches, and run it against your own failing case before the notice arrives.

## Activepieces as a Swappable Model Layer in Workflows

Don't mistake Activepieces for an Inkling 2 Small alternative; it isn't a model.

It's what lets you swap the model behind a step without rewriting the process around it.

For most teams it comes down to three: DeepSeek V4 Flash if you want the same job done cheaper, Inkling itself if you want the same family with better factual recall, and Claude Opus 5 if a wrong answer costs real money. The full lineup in this post also covers GLM-5.2, MiniMax M3, Kimi K3, Qwen3.8-Max and Gemini 3.6 Flash.

Is there a cheaper alternative to Inkling-Small?

Yes. DeepSeek V4 Flash pricing is $0.14 in and $0.28 out per million tokens, against Inkling-Small's $0.30 and $1.20, so output is roughly four times cheaper. MiniMax M3 matches Inkling-Small exactly at $0.30 and $1.20 below 512K of input. If you are trying to get your cost per resolution down, the model line item is rarely the biggest one. Inkling-Small's knowledge index is negative and its parent's is positive, so the cheapest real fix is a step up inside the same family: same licence, same tooling, roughly 3.4x the output price. Opus 5 costs a lot more and is the one to reach for when a wrong answer is a refund, a compliance issue or a churned customer.

results.title: Inkling 2 Mini Benchmarks, Cost and Capabilities | Vals AI
results.content:
On the Vals Index, Mini scores 46.46%, up 17.5 points from the original Inkling. It improves on the original across 13 of 18 shared benchmarks.
   On Vibe Code Bench, it scores 77.92%, up from the original Inkling’s 19.21%. It scores 56.54% on Finance Agent v2.1 at about 5 minutes per task, and 37.92% on SWE-bench Multimodal.
   Mini reaches 96% of Inkling 2 Small‘s Vibe Code Bench score (77.92% versus 81.55%) and 97% of its SAGE score (85.89% versus 88.57%).

Thinking Machines says Mini has 26B parameters, with 5.4B active on each token, and twelve of its 24 layers run three times on each token, using more computation per token instead of more tokens. It has a 1M-token context window and supports 1M output tokens. The weights are available on Hugging Face and Ollama under Apache 2.0.
